recognize_zh: 一顆淋巴球胞質豐富而淡藍，內含數顆粗大紫紅色嗜天青顆粒（azurophilic granules），核偏向一側、染色質濃縮，是典型的大型顆粒淋巴球（LGL）。
features: Lymphocyte with abundant pale blue cytoplasm, larger than a small lymphocyte
Several coarse, discrete azurophilic (red-purple) cytoplasmic granules
Slightly eccentric, oval nucleus with condensed chromatin
Cytoplasmic border molded by adjacent red cells
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear at high power shows a lymphocyte with abundant pale blue cytoplasm containing several coarse discrete azurophilic granules, and a slightly eccentric oval nucleus with condensed chromatin without nucleoli. The morphology is that of a large granular lymphocyte. A single LGL is normal; T-cell large granular lymphocytic leukemia requires a sustained LGL count usually above 2 x 10^9/L with a clonal CD3+/CD8+/CD57+ population, TCR clonality and often STAT3 mutation.

ddx.dx: Chronic lymphoproliferative disorder of NK cells
ddx.vs: NK-cell LGLs look identical but are surface CD3-negative, CD16/CD56-positive without TCR rearrangement.
Reactive LGL expansions are transient and polyclonal, which requires follow-up flow cytometry and TCR studies to separate.
Reactive lymphocytes have deeply basophilic cytoplasm scalloping around red cells and usually lack discrete coarse azurophilic granules.
Aggressive NK-cell leukemia cells are larger and more atypical with nucleoli, EBV positive and associated with a fulminant clinical course.
